pr_title: sysext: Set SELinux context for overlay hierarchies mountpoints
pr_body:
See: https://github.com/coreos/fedora-coreos-tracker/issues/1744
See: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/31404

Fixes: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/34387

---

With this change, I get the correct SELinux label for `/usr` with sysexts:

```
# ls -alhZd /etc /usr /opt
drwxr-xr-x. 86 root root system_u:object_r:etc_t:s0 8.0K Sep 13 16:50 /etc
lrwxrwxrwx.  1 root root system_u:object_r:usr_t:s0    7 Jan  1  1970 /opt -> var/opt
drwxr-xr-x.  1 root root system_u:object_r:usr_t:s0   60 Sep 13 22:15 /usr
```

It's however evidently not correct as it hard codes the label instead of using the one from the destination path.

I haven't figured out how I should do it properly yet. I tried doing:

```
+       r = mac_selinux_create_file_prepare(op->hierarchy, 0700);
+       if (r < 0)
+                return log_error_errno(r, "Failed to setup SELinux label for '%s' -> '%s': %m", meta_path, op->hierarchy);
+
         r = mkdir_p(meta_path, 0700);
         if (r < 0)
                 return log_error_errno(r, "Failed to make directory '%s': %m", meta_path);
+       mac_selinux_create_file_clear();
```

but that did not work, thus the draft.

issue_context.title: Incorrect SELinux label for `/usr` when using sysexts
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

systemd-256.5-1.fc41.x86_64

### Used distribution

Fedora 41

### Linux kernel version used

6.11.0-0.rc5.43.fc41.x86_64

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemd-sysext

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

Merging sysexts should not impact the SELinux label of `/usr`.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

On a Fedora CoreOS 41 system, I added a sysext and merged it. The resulting `/usr` mount is incorrectly labeled:

```
# ls -alhZ /usr/
total 76K
drwxr-xr-x.  1 root root unconfined_u:object_r:user_tmp_t:s0   60 Sep 12 10:48 .
drwxr-xr-x. 12 root root system_u:object_r:root_t:s0         4.0K Jan  1  1970 ..
drwxr-xr-x.  2 root root unconfined_u:object_r:user_tmp_t:s0   80 Sep 12 10:48 .systemd-sysext
drwxr-xr-x.  1 root root system_u:object_r:bin_t:s0            48 Aug 29 18:23 bin
drwxr-xr-x. 86 root root system_u:object_r:etc_t:s0          4.0K Jan  1  1970 etc
drwxr-xr-x.  2 root root system_u:object_r:usr_t:s0            27 Jan  1  1970 games
drwxr-xr-x.  2 root root system_u:object_r:usr_t:s0            27 Jan  1  1970 include
drwxr-xr-x.  1 root root system_u:object_r:lib_t:s0            58 Sep 12 09:39 lib
drwxr-xr-x. 42 root root system_u:object_r:lib_t:s0           20K Jan  1  1970 lib64
drwxr-xr-x. 30 root root system_u:object_r:bin_t:s0          1.9K Jan  1  1970 libexec
lrwxrwxrwx.  1 root root system_u:object_r:usr_t:s0            15 Jan  1  1970 local -> ../var/usrlocal
drwxr-xr-x.  2 root root system_u:object_r:bin_t:s0          9.6K Jan  1  1970 sbin
drwxr-xr-x. 87 root root system_u:object_r:usr_t:s0          1.7K Jan  1  1970 share
drwxr-xr-x.  4 root root system_u:object_r:usr_t:s0            63 Jan  1  1970 src
lrwxrwxrwx.  1 root root system_u:object_r:usr_t:s0            10 Jan  1  1970 tmp -> ../var/tmp
```

From my understanding of the code, it looks like systemd-sysexts creates `/run/systemd/sysext` (https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/src/sysext/sysext.c#L1805) and then sets up / merges sysext mounts form there (https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/src/sysext/sysext.c#L1497).

Thus it's likely that the SELinux contexts from there "leaks" to the final `/usr` mount.

The SELinux context matches the one in `/run/user/0/systemd/`:
```
# ls -alhdZ /run/user/0/systemd/
drwxr-xr-x. 5 root root unconfined_u:object_r:user_tmp_t:s0 140 Sep 12 10:27 /run/user/0/systemd/
```

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Boot a Fedora CoreOS 41 system. This might also be reproducible on a classic dnf Fedora 41 system but I've not checked yet.
2. Add a sysext
3. Run `systemd-sysext merge`
4. Run `ls -alZ /usr`

See:
- Fedora CoreOS: https://github.com/coreos/fedora-coreos-tracker/issues/1744
- A likely previous report of this issue: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/31404

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

_No response_
comments:
One option would be to make sure that the SELinux labels of the files/directories created during the sysexts merging process are either:
- set to the default one from the policy for the final expected paths
- or set to the ones from the current system before merging the sysexts: `chcon --reference /usr /run/systemd/sysext/usr`

A workaround for this issue is to let the `systemd-sysext.service` merge the sysexts instead of doing it manually as it will run under a "more correct" SELinux context and will thus create the `/usr` mount point with something that is readable by most processes:

```
[root@cosa-devsh ~]# systemd-sysext unmerge
Unmerged '/usr'.

[root@cosa-devsh ~]# systemd-sysext status
HIERARCHY EXTENSIONS SINCE
/opt      none       -    
/usr      none       -    

[root@cosa-devsh ~]# ls -alhZ /usr/
total 100K
drwxr-xr-x. 12 root root system_u:object_r:usr_t:s0   224 Jan  1  1970 .
drwxr-xr-x. 12 root root system_u:object_r:root_t:s0 4.0K Jan  1  1970 ..
...

[root@cosa-devsh ~]# systemctl restart systemd-sysext.service 

[root@cosa-devsh ~]# systemd-sysext status
HIERARCHY EXTENSIONS SINCE                      
/opt      none       -                          
/usr      erofs      Thu 2024-09-12 11:37:27 UTC

[root@cosa-devsh ~]# ls -alhZ /usr/
total 76K
drwxr-xr-x.  1 root root system_u:object_r:tmpfs_t:s0   60 Sep 12 11:37 .
drwxr-xr-x. 12 root root system_u:object_r:root_t:s0  4.0K Jan  1  1970 ..
drwxr-xr-x.  2 root root system_u:object_r:tmpfs_t:s0   80 Sep 12 11:37 .systemd-sysext
...
```
Shouldn't the policy be changed to ensure /run/systemd/sysext is created with the expected label instead?
We can probably do that as well. I'll give it a try. Is `/run/systemd/sysext` the directory that ends up being used as `/usr`?
it should be `/run/systemd/sysext/overlay/usr` and `/run/systemd/sysext/overlay/opt`  and  `/run/systemd/sysext/overlay/etc`  respectively for the default hierarchies we handle
hmm, we do have code to apply labels based on a future path to some inode we create. I think it would make sense to use that here so that the policy can stay simple.
We run into the same problem on openSUSE MicroOS.
I've tested this on Rawhide with systemd v257-rc3 and things looks good. Thanks!

review_comments: misses access mode, i.e. O_RDONLY or O_PATH or so
We should probably close this fd?
use `_cleanup_close_` here. And we also use `-EBADF` as value for "uninitialized fd".
hmm, this looks wrong, the path of this meta file is not the path of the hierarchy itself, but something further below.

also, writing the file here first, and then opening it again to set the label kinda misseses the point of pinning things.

I'd prefer if we could do that as one. i.e. let's switch over to using the write_string_file_full_label() flavour of calls for this, which combine the write logic and the labelling into one. (But note that I cleaned up the naming of those functions in PR #34781, hence please look at the API in that version. Hopefully this gets merged quickly).

write_string_file_full_label() lacks the ability to override the path looked up in the db so that it can be different than the file actually created. But it should be trivial to extend the call with an extra option for that.
